correctness.rationale: An inverse start is precisely an eight-letter palindrome, and deleting its final four letters is the inverse for the stated reversal channel. Two such starts separated by h=1 or 2 imply y_j=y_(j+2h) on the common reflection range by composition. For h=1 and h=2 the required remaining substrings after deleting four are equal since the period divides four (the compared positions are j=4,…,3+h and j+4 in local coordinates). One representative per distinct parent has spacing at least three in the n−3 start positions. For the period-three witness with a≠b, each start i divisible by three sees the palindrome aabaabaa; for i<j the deletion at i gives b at output index i+4 while the deletion at j leaves a there. The later legal start ensures that coordinate and y_(i+8) exist. This also covers n=4, when there is just one start, and uses only equality of letters, so q≥2 suffices. value.rationale: The exact worst-case number of distinct parents is a natural local decoding ambiguity, not a count of syntactic edit positions. Length four is the first case outside the earlier uniform formula for blocks not divisible by four. Even though the sharp upper bound follows from known local collisions, proving that one receives that many distinct parents in every length gives a substantive exact invariant and identifies a simple witness. This is not a claim about codebook optimality or about multiple errors.
